restaurants.notes: SOURCE METHOD: fetched raw HTML of every page on danvilleharvest.com with curl -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" (site nav has only 5 pages: /, /menu, /events, /contact, /reservations; /about, /gallery, /press, /our-story, /private-events all return 404). Extracted , data-src, srcset, og:image, Squarespace assetUrl JSON and CSS background-image; resolved and de-duplicated to canonical Squarespace CDN bases; requested each at ?format=2500w. Every URL below was HEAD-checked with curl -sIL (all 200) and then downloaded and measured with Pillow, and every image was visually inspected before being described. No Instagram/Facebook CDN URLs are included. FORMAT NEGOTIATION: images.squarespace-cdn.com content-negotiates. With Accept: image/webp it returns image/webp (e.g. Harvest_6_15_23-94 = 711,138 B WEBP); with a plain jpeg Accept it returns image/jpeg (772,706 B). The content_type/bytes recorded here are the JPEG/PNG variant. Pixel dimensions are identical either way. The originals were uploaded at 2000 px on the long edge, so ?format=2500w returns the full 2000x1333 (or 1333x2000) original - there is nothing larger. OWN PHOTOGRAPHY: all 24 restaurant photos on the site come from one professional shoot, filenames Harvest_6_15_23-N.jpg (shot 15 June 2023). Full set of N used on the site: 1, 9, 40, 47, 56, 64, 70, 73, 85, 86, 91, 94, 106, 127, 128, 130, 131, 134, 139, 152, 156, 158, 159, 160. All are included below. The site has no gallery/lightbox page holding additional images. OG:IMAGE PER PAGE (all verified 200, served from static1.squarespace.com at ?format=1500w; note the site declares them with an http:// scheme, https works fine): / -> Harvest_6_15_23-160.jpg (recorded above as og_image); /menu -> .../6494f6b74cda395e3373f030/1687484087914/Harvest_6_15_23-64.jpg; /events -> .../6494f6ca6d6d73138103e1d3/1687484106288/Harvest_6_15_23-128.jpg; /contact -> .../6494f6f7f3a6a6170b0b3cab/1687484151307/Harvest_6_15_23-1.jpg; /reservations -> .../6494f69dcfb66a798e27a618/1687484061743/Harvest_6_15_23-156.jpg. LOGOS: two official variants, both RGBA transparent PNG and both LIGHT-coloured, so neither will read on a white directory card - header wordmark Danville_Harvest_conceptlogo.png is pure white (579x115), footer mark Harvest_yellow.png is cream (350x201, barn + tree illustration above the wordmark). A BLACK-on-white version of the same barn logo (992x618 PNG) is hosted third-party at danvillesocial.com and is included below as the usable light-background variant. NAME HISTORY (important for dated photos): the restaurant opened in 2016 as "Almanac" and was renamed "Harvest"/"Danville Harvest" over a trademark issue - same owners, same 500 Hartz Ave building (confirmed on the architect's project page, laraarchitecture.squarespace.com/harvest-restaurant: "Harvest (formerly called Almanac) was a complete renovation of a 3000-square-foot restaurant... The historic building situated on a prominent corner of Danville's downtown district"). Any third-party photo showing an "almanac" sign or white-subway-tile / Tolix-chair interior is this restaurant pre-refresh, not a different business. EXTERIOR / HARTZ + CHURCH CORNER: confirmed the building sits on the Hartz Ave & Church St corner. The four best corner shots are the restaurant's own: Harvest_6_15_23-94 (golden hour, tight on the corner sign), -156 (blue hour, whole corner lit), -106 (wide, from across the intersection) and -152 (side patio at night). The one press exterior found is Food Gal's HarvestExterior.jpg (night, corner, diners on the patio, USPS mailbox) but it is only 760x427. PRESS SEARCHED: danvillesanramon.com (no Harvest-specific article; the 4 May 2026 Rancho Cantina piece only name-checks "Danville Harvest at 500 Hartz Ave." and its photos are of 501 Hartz across the street). Diablo Magazine's site returned HTTP 429 to every request and could not be read. Hoodline, Patch and Bay Area Telegraph searches returned nothing on this restaurant. Yelp and Tripadvisor were not used (403/blocked, and user photos are last resort). The architect's page cites two 2016 print pieces I could not retrieve: East Bay Times, 22 Sep 2016, "Plenty to Love at Danville's Almanac Bistro" and Diablo Magazine, Oct 2016, "A Sweet Success: Farmers Almanac offers Bay Area cuisine with a shot of Southern comfort". VERIFIED BUT NOT LISTED BELOW (all HEAD-200 and measured, omitted to keep the list usable): - Food Gal (2018 review, https://www.foodgal.com/2018/05/a-taste-of-the-seasons-at-danville-harvest/) dish photos, author's own captions: Cauliflower.jpg 760x517 304,866B "a simple yet striking roasted cauliflower"; Wagyu.jpg 760x474 439,677B sliced wagyu sirloin with arugula and corn succotash; Lamb.jpg 740x1079 667,459B lamb with carrot puree; BeetSoup.jpg 760x658 424,955B; PorkTenderloin.jpg 680x946 604,450B; ShrimpKamut.jpg 760x522 386,612B; BasilPotdeCreme.jpg 660x955 690,012B; ChessPie.jpg 760x496 400,090B. All under https://www.foodgal.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/. These are 2018 dishes; most are no longer on the June 2026 menus, so use with care. - Lara Architecture project page, https://laraarchitecture.squarespace.com/harvest-restaurant (all under https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/65b48a4b1e423855b3c1546a/): 776d0644-5a9d-45f9-9d5f-b8d70481b30f/row-of-dining-tables-with-a-view-of-the-open-kitchen-in-the-background.jpg 1400x2100 213,321B; 0f2a761d-aedb-4bbe-8aec-536e9f8d486b/built-in-tuffted-leather-bench-seat-table-in-corner-next-to-a-wall-of-windows-at-harvest-restaurant-in-danville.jpg 1400x2418 344,542B; 36962d95-748b-47d1-9c08-8561ce4ecf48/diners-sitting-at-countertop-that-faces-into-the-restaurant-kitchen-as-they-talk-with-a-smiling-chef.jpg 1800x1295 334,048B; 37a47966-9c32-47bc-877a-0d579a0440ac/interior-entry-area-at-harvest-restaurant.jpg 1400x2024 257,680B; c6fa79ab-e599-41f3-a017-7f8bdf242664/entry-with-wood-table-and-chandelier-at-harvest-restaurant.jpg 1400x2075 324,715B; 64ee91f0-7a0f-4517-b3b4-2aae7aae60f9/two-chefs-work-side-by-side-in-open-kitchen-with-view-of-diners-inside-the-dining-room-at-harvest-restaurant-in-Danville.jpg 1800x1200 312,941B. - danvillesocial.com directory listing (https://www.danvillesocial.com/directory/danville-harvest/) also hosts five 2019-era amateur customer snapshots under https://www.danvillesocial.com/php_partials/uploads/2019/01/: Danville-Harvest-1.jpg 1000x1000 (deviled eggs on a periwinkle plate, an "almanac" menu visible), -2.jpg 750x1000 (charcuterie board, dim), -3.jpg 750x1000 (eggs benedict), -4.jpg 1000x562 (cobb salad), -5.jpg 750x1000 (entry doors under an "almanac" sign). Low quality / obsolete branding - last resort only. CAVEATS: rights were not cleared for any third-party image; Food Gal and Lara Architecture photos are the photographers'/publishers' and would need permission. The Lara Architecture set documents the 2016 build-out (Almanac signage, white subway tile, Tolix chairs) - the dining rooms have since been re-clad in chevron reclaimed wood with leather nailhead chairs and linen drapes, so those photos no longer match the current room. The chef pictured in Food Gal's TimHumphrey.jpg is Tim Humphrey, exec chef in 2018; the current exec chef is Noe Briseno, so do not caption it as the current chef. No current-day chef or staff portrait exists on the restaurant's own site.

images.description: Golden-hour exterior of the corner building, shot from the sidewalk. The glassed-in porch dining room with weathered timber posts fills the frame, the large painted white-on-grey 'harvest' sign hangs on the corner, cafe string lights run overhead, shingle roof and navy patio umbrellas above, a bed of blooming lavender and ornamental grasses along the low stucco wall, a sycamore trunk at left. Site alt text: 'Danville Harvest Exterior'. Best daytime exterior available.

Blue-hour / twilight exterior of the whole corner: deep blue sky, the yellow clapboard building glowing warm from inside, string lights strung across the patio, the 'harvest' sign lit on the corner fence, navy umbrellas, uplit planting bed, blue USPS mailbox and a wine barrel at left, brick-banded crosswalk in the foreground. og:image of the /reservations page. Strongest evening hero.

Wide establishing shot taken from across the intersection at dusk, showing the full corner of Hartz Ave and Church St: the yellow single-storey building with dark shingle roof under mature street trees, the 'harvest' sign on the porch fence, navy and cream umbrellas, a US flag on the neighbouring facade, blue USPS mailbox, two green trash bins, the brick crosswalk and street in the foreground. Site alt text: 'The view of Danville Harvest as seen from across the street.'

The side patio at night: rows of empty slatted-wood tables and chairs on a paved terrace, a retractable white awning and cafe string lights overhead, wall-mounted overhead heaters, the yellow clapboard wall with a run of French doors glowing warm, guests visible seated inside, picket fence and ornamental grasses along the sidewalk edge. Site alt text: 'The side patio area as seen at night.'

Daytime patio-dining scene on a weathered wood outdoor table: a glazed bone-in pork chop over sweet-potato puree with greens and chutney on a rustic cream plate, a coupe cocktail full of cloudy orange liquid at right, a tall lemon-and-mint highball at left, a plate of fried croquettes with citrus salad at lower right, a bud vase of pink and magenta blooms, parked cars and green street trees blurred behind. Site alt text: 'Drinks and entrees on our outside patio'. Good for conveying the sidewalk-patio experience.

Back dining area looking down a long row of two-top tables: tan leather nailhead-trim chairs, wood table tops set with dark folded napkins and single pink peonies in glass bud vases, black industrial dome pendants, floor-to-ceiling linen drapes gathered and tied with rope, blue tufted banquettes on the right, and a white-framed pass-through window with stacked crockery on the left. Site alt text: 'Back Dining Area'. Best interior hero.

Wide, evenly lit view of the main back dining room: a chevron/herringbone reclaimed-wood feature wall hung with two round mirrors and small framed photographs, a long grey tufted banquette beneath it, tan leather nailhead chairs at wood tables with pink peonies, tall multi-pane windows with linen drapes at left looking onto the street, black dome pendants, polished concrete floor. Site alt text: 'Our main dining area in the back of our restaurant. Great for private events.'

The full bar, shot square-on: tiered timber back-bar shelving packed with whiskey and spirit bottles and lit from beneath, suspended blackened-steel racks holding more bottles and hanging stemware, a bank of draft taps and a small oak barrel on the counter, a wall-mounted TV, sage-green upholstered swivel bar stools along a thick dark wood bar top, glass-front under-bar coolers and a wine fridge. Supports the 'largest whiskey selection in the Tri-Valley' claim.

Front bar-lounge room looking out from behind the bar top: sage-green bar chairs along a thick wood counter in the foreground, a caramel leather button-tufted banquette running along the far wall with wood two-tops in front of it, chevron reclaimed-wood wall panels, a suspended glassware rack, a small chandelier, a TV, a trailing pothos plant, framed pictures, and windows onto the street. Site alt text: 'The view of our front dining area with full bar and tables.'

Vertical dining-room shot down a row of wood tables set with dark napkins and pink peonies in bud vases, tan leather nailhead chairs, black dome pendants, gathered linen drapes at right, and a large weathered metal 'COOK' sign on the back wall above an opening to the front room and a street-facing window. Portrait orientation - good for a mobile or sidebar slot, too dark and tall for a wide hero. og:image of the /events page.

Moody vertical view into the curtained private-dining nook: heavy linen drapes tied back on both sides framing a row of set tables with tan leather chairs and pink peonies, the chevron wood wall and grey banquette at the far end, warm pendant light pooling on the tables, the pass-through window and shelving glowing at right. Deliberately dark and atmospheric. Site alt text: 'Our back dining area. Perfect for private parties. Links to Events page.'

The restaurant's own homepage hero and site-wide og:image: two deeply seared scallops on a bed of creamy risotto with diced vegetables, crowned with a tall tangle of red-stemmed micro greens, in a dark blue-black ceramic bowl on a walnut table; a glass of white wine, a second plated dish and a lime wedge blurred behind. Shallow depth of field, warm side light.

A thick block of glazed braised short rib set on a nest of wide fettuccine and wilted spinach in a dark speckled bowl, topped with a crisp tangle of fried onion strings and lemon zest, on an outdoor wood table; a pink grapefruit cocktail, a green cocktail, magenta and pink blooms in bud vases and a parked car all blurred behind. Site alt text: 'Glazed Short Ribs'. Matches the menu's Braised Short Ribs and Short Rib Bites.

Overhead three-quarter shot of two dishes and a drink on a wood table: a seasonal salad in a dark speckled bowl (butter lettuce, mango, blueberries, strawberries, cucumber, shaved onion, flax seed) beside a terracotta plate of golden fried chicken with lemon wheels, rosemary, green beans and cream sauce, with a rocks glass of an old-fashioned garnished with a citrus twist between them. Site alt text: 'Our fresh seasonal salad and fried chicken.'

Action shot: a hand holding a kitchen blowtorch, blue flame lit, searing a rosemary sprig planted in a mound of craggy golden fried chicken with lemon wheels and green beans in a pale cream sauce on a terracotta-orange plate; a bright red cocktail in a cut-glass tumbler at left, a bowl of chopped salad at right, dark slate-blue background. Site alt text: 'Fried Chicken Dinner. Links to Dinner menu in a new browser tab.' Most dramatic of the food images.

A tall, glossy glazed bone-in pork chop resting on wilted spinach and a swipe of sweet-potato/squash puree, topped with a chunky apple-onion chutney and micro herbs, with a pool of dark jus alongside, on a rustic speckled cream plate; a stemmed glass of beer or wine and folded napkin blurred behind, warm window light across a wood table. og:image of the /menu page.

A crisp tempura-battered stuffed squash blossom propped on a nest of frisee and micro greens with blistered cherry tomatoes and green beans, over a broad pool of orange romesco-style sauce dusted with paprika, on a rectangular white ceramic plate. Clean, high-contrast subject on a simple plate - the easiest of the food shots to crop or cut out. Site alt text: 'Squash Blossom Brunch Dish. Links to Brunch menu in a new browser tab.'

A cheese and charcuterie board laid out on a long wooden paddle: blue cheese, wedges of hard and semi-hard cheese, sliced green apple, dried apricots, spiced nuts, a green olive, pickled red onion, toasted crostini and a small copper ramekin of honey; a pink cocktail with a lime wheel at upper left, an empty teal plate, and a white plate of golden fried croquettes with grapefruit-and-fennel citrus salad at right, all on a weathered grey outdoor table. Good 'shareable plates / happy hour' image.

A hand pours amber whiskey from a glass carafe into a fluted crystal rocks glass holding a large clear ice cube and a citrus twist, wisps of smoke curling off the surface, on a dark polished wood bar; magenta chrysanthemums in a mason jar and a folded napkin with cutlery behind, the pourer's red-and-white floral sleeve at right. Site alt text: 'Manhattan Cocktail'. Best bar-programme image.

A vivid ruby-red cocktail in a cut-crystal rocks glass garnished with a rosemary sprig, sharply lit against a dark slate-blue background; a coupe of dark cherry-garnished Manhattan-style cocktail at left, a cloudy amber sour out of focus at right, a plate of grilled asparagus salad and croquettes with citrus salad in the lower frame. Strong colour, dark simple backdrop - crops well.

Two golden seared scallops on herbed risotto with halved cherry tomatoes and a spray of red-stemmed micro greens in a dark ceramic bowl on a wood table, another plate and a wine glass blurred behind. Same dish and setup as Harvest_6_15_23-160 but lit darker and moodier; use -160 instead unless a low-key version is wanted. Site alt text: 'Scallop Lunch dish. Links to Lunch Menu in a new browser tab.'

Very shallow-focus table scene: a grilled asparagus salad with draped prosciutto, shaved hard cheese, pine nuts and mixed leaves on a white rectangular plate in the foreground (partly cropped by the frame edge), with an Aperol-style orange spritz, a dark cocktail, a plate of croquettes with citrus salad and a napkin-and-fork setting all softly blurred behind. Atmospheric rather than a clean dish shot. Site alt text: 'A fresh asparagus and prosciutto dish.'

Overhead, dramatically side-lit dessert: a custard (creme brulee style) in a white ramekin dusted heavily with powdered sugar and topped with a single strawberry slice, sitting on a walnut serving board scattered with more powdered sugar alongside two shards of biscotti/shortbread; a dark Manhattan-style cocktail in a coupe with a citrus twist at upper left, a knife and napkin at lower left, a water glass upper right, dark wood table. Site alt text: 'Our creme brulee dessert dish'. Note: no dessert menu is published on the site.

Table-setting detail on a reclaimed wood table: two place settings of stacked speckled plates with folded charcoal napkins and silverware, a single lilac chrysanthemum in a dimpled amber bud vase and a jar of magenta and cream chrysanthemums, backlit by the white-framed multi-pane porch windows and the yellow clapboard wall behind. Calm, low-clutter brand image with a simple background - good for a card or section break. og:image of the /contact page.

Official site header logo: horizontal wordmark, small spaced capitals 'DANVILLE' above a large rough typewriter-style lowercase 'harvest'. Pure WHITE artwork on a transparent background (PNG, RGBA) - invisible on white, needs a dark or photographic backdrop. Appears in the header of all five site pages.

Official site footer logo: a hand-drawn barn with an open door and a small tree on a ground line, with 'DANVILLE' set into the ground line at left and the large typewriter-style 'harvest' wordmark beneath. Cream / off-white artwork on a transparent background (PNG, RGBA) - also needs a dark backdrop. Appears in the footer of all five site pages.

WARNING - STOCK PHOTO, NOT DANVILLE HARVEST. Licensed Unsplash image (filename unsplash-image-xIFbDeGcy44.jpg) used as a decorative section background on the menu page: two shallow stone-coloured bowls of a vegetable/crudo dish on a rough wooden table with a glass of white wine, a glass of red, a jar of blue wildflowers and an antique fork. Recorded only so it is not mistaken for the restaurant's own photography - do not use it on the directory listing.

Press photo (Food Gal review, May 2018) of the Hartz Ave / Church St corner at night: the yellow clapboard building lit up, cafe string lights strung over the front patio, the black-and-white 'harvest' sign on the picket fence, guests dining at tables under furled and open umbrellas, the blue USPS mailbox and sycamore trunk at left, a second 'harvest' sign over the side entrance. Article caption: 'Located on a corner with plenty of outside seating for those balmy Danville evenings.' Only 760x427, so not usable as a hero - the restaurant's own -156 and -106 cover the same view at 2000 px. Rights not cleared.

Press photo (Food Gal, May 2018) of the dining room: a black-and-white damask curtain tied back with twine on a timber post, dark button-tufted leather banquette, wood tables, metal Tolix-style chairs, a rolling library ladder, wood-plank ceiling with track lighting, and a fiddle-leaf fig by the service station. HISTORICAL - the room has since been redecorated (plain linen drapes, tan leather nailhead chairs, chevron wood wall); do not present as current. Article caption: 'The dining room.'

Press photo (Food Gal, May 2018) of six golden-fried hushpuppy spheres on a periwinkle-blue rectangular plate with a chive-topped quenelle of butter/aioli behind, on a wood table. Article caption: 'Hushpuppies that never leave the menu' - the hushpuppies are still on the current dinner, lunch and brunch menus, so this is the only photograph found anywhere of the restaurant's signature dish. The restaurant's own site has no hushpuppy shot. Rights not cleared.

Press portrait (Food Gal, May 2018) of a smiling bearded chef in a white chef coat embroidered 'harvest' on the chest and his name on the pocket, standing at the kitchen pass with the steel equipment racks behind him. Article caption: 'Chef Tim Humphrey.' DO NOT USE AS A CURRENT CHEF PORTRAIT - the executive chef today is Noe Briseno. Recorded only as the sole staff photograph found; the restaurant's own site publishes none.

BLACK-on-white version of the restaurant's barn logo - the same artwork as the official cream Harvest_yellow.png (line-drawn barn with open door, small tree, 'DANVILLE' in the ground line, big typewriter 'harvest' beneath) rendered in solid black on a white field at 992x618. Hosted by the danvillesocial.com local directory, alt text 'Harvest restaurant in Danville CA'. This is the only dark-on-light logo variant found and is the practical choice for a white directory card, but it is a third-party copy - ask the restaurant for the original asset before publishing.

Professional architectural photo from the project page of Lara Architecture, who designed the restaurant: a server in apron and dress carrying plates down the timber steps of the front porch onto the sunlit patio, where guests sit at wood tables under big cream umbrellas behind a low picket fence with lavender planted along it, mature sycamores overhead, the yellow clapboard facade behind. No signage visible so it does not date itself, but it documents the 2016 build-out (then trading as Almanac). Best third-party daytime patio image. Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's photo of the front entrance: a dark steel awning with cut-metal letters spelling 'almanac' over open dark-framed French doors set into the pale yellow clapboard facade, lantern sconces either side, dappled sycamore shade and blue sky above. HISTORICAL - shows the building under its original name before the rename to Harvest, so it cannot be used as a current exterior. Useful only as evidence of the building/facade design. Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's photo of the bar shot square-on in daylight: white subway-tiled back wall, suspended blackened-steel racks holding spirits and rows of stemware, a bank of draft taps on a stainless plinth, back-bar bottle shelves, a white jug of sunflowers and a bowl of lemons on the thick wood counter, sage-green bar chairs across the foreground. Same bar as the restaurant's own -134 but brighter and pre-refresh (2016 build). Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's photo of the open kitchen from the dining room: cooks working behind a long white counter under custom blackened-steel equipment racks stacked with pans, baskets, crockery and bread, big black dome pendants and heat lamps overhead, white subway tile throughout, and a row of wood two-top tables with metal Tolix chairs and small potted succulents in the foreground. The clearest existing view of the on-display kitchen. HISTORICAL (2016 build-out, pre-rename). Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

Architect's wide interior of the main dining room: dark green button-tufted leather banquettes against a grey wall hung with two round mirrors and framed pictures (the same mirrors still hang on today's chevron wood wall), heavy reclaimed timber posts and beams under a wood-plank ceiling, black articulated wall lamps and dome pendants, and along the right a white subway-tiled kitchen counter with a reclaimed-wood shelf, faced by wood tables and Tolix chairs on polished concrete. HISTORICAL (2016 build-out, pre-rename) - the walls and seating have since changed. Rights are the architect's/photographer's.

chamber.name: Danville Area Chamber of Commerce
chamber.contact: 117-E Town and Country Drive, Danville, CA 94526 | (925) 837-4400 | office@danvilleareachamber.com (general) | events@danvilleareachamber.com (events/sponsorships). Staff (per chamber staff page): Amy Millington, President (president@danvilleareachamber.com); Noemi Chojnacka, Member Services Manager | Office (x1801); Karen Stevenot, Events Manager (x1804). Note: the Tri-Valley Chamber Alliance page still lists Judy Lloyd as President/CEO, so that page appears out of date. Social: Instagram @danvilleareachamber, Facebook /DanvilleAreaChamber, LinkedIn. Member portal + public event calendar: https://business.danvilleareachamber.com/
chamber.programs: Founded New Year's Eve 1948; serves Danville, Alamo, Blackhawk and Diablo. Roughly 500-600 member businesses, 4 staff, 15-member board (per Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance). Member benefits (per Why Join page): online business directory listing, Member-to-Member Deals, newsletter features, social media promotion, ribbon cuttings, monthly mixers, referral/leads groups (Sunrise Alliance, Diablo Business Network), free small-business workshops, private meeting room access, grant navigation, signature-event access. MOST RELEVANT PROGRAMS FOR THE DISTRICT: (1) Sip & Stroll - the chamber's 20-year signature wine-stroll, Thursday May 7 2026, 5:30-8:30pm, ~35 participating businesses across downtown Danville AND the Danville Livery, $65 tasting / $20 designated driver, includes commemorative wine glass, tote, live music and FREE TROLLEY between downtown and the Livery. Businesses join by submitting the 'Become a Participating Business' form to events@danvilleareachamber.com and choosing a sponsorship level. (2) Fall Hallo-Wine - Oct 28 2026, downtown (chamber-run fall counterpart to Sip & Stroll; earlier years ran as Flavors of Fall, Oktoberfest and Fall Rock & Stroll). (3) Lighting of the Old Oak Tree - Nov 27 2026, downtown (49th edition was Nov 28 2025, program 5pm, tree lit ~6:30pm, on Diablo Rd between W El Pintado and I-680; run with the Town). (4) Paws & Claws in Downtown Danville - Dec 10 2026. (5) Passport to Wellness - June 13 2026. (6) Other: State of the Town, Community Awards Celebration/Gala, Women's Enterprise Initiative, historically two annual arts & crafts fairs (Summerfest in June and Fallfest in October). The chamber does NOT run a restaurant week; its dining-adjacent vehicle is the seasonal wine/beer stroll series. Member of the Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance (trivalleychambers.org) alongside Dublin, Livermore Valley, Pleasanton and San Ramon chambers.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - Economic Development Division
town_orgs.note: Primary town contact. Melysa Vander Mel, Supervisor of Economic Development (also listed elsewhere as Economic Development Specialist), 925-314-3379, mvandermel@danville.ca.gov. Offers: Business Concierge (guides businesses through development review), Business Boost Grant Program, Business Funding Support described as grants to market businesses OR to fund collaborative community events (directly relevant - a four-restaurant district event is exactly the collaborative-event framing), market analysis/demographics, business library, sign permits, TEMPORARY OUTDOOR PERMITS, and downtown employee parking permits.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - 'Live Locally' branding & marketing campaign
town_orgs.note: The Town's official place brand, tagline 'Live Locally' / 'So much to do...so little time.' Includes custom logos, color palette and photography, and the official hashtag #LiveLocallyDanville, which residents, business owners and visitors are explicitly asked to use. Rolled out across all Town digital and print channels. Contact for business use: Melysa Vander Mel.

town_orgs.name: Discover Danville (Town of Danville web app)
town_orgs.note: Free web-based walking-tour app - no download or login. Maps historic landmarks, local shops and restaurants, shows historical 'what used to be' photos, and has a dog-friendly filter. Explicitly built to drive foot traffic to small businesses. Also used as the delivery channel for Small Business Saturday specials, decorated-storefront voting and the Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt. A district listing/route here is a free, high-leverage ask.

town_orgs.name: California Main Street / Main Street America designation
town_orgs.note: Danville was officially designated both a California Main Street and Main Street America affiliate community (announced alongside Small Business Saturday, Nov 29 2025). Mayor Renee Morgan framed it as recognition of the Town's investment in local business. Useful hook for positioning a new dining district as part of the Main Street story.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - Recreation, Arts & Community Services (RACS)
town_orgs.note: 925-314-3400, recreation@danville.ca.gov. Runs the Town's free entertainment programming: Music at the Plaza and 'At the Plaza' series at Prospect Park Plaza (downtown), Music in the Park, Moonlight Movies, Kidchella, Art in the Park, Howl-o-Ween, Spooktacular. Also operates the Village Theatre & Art Gallery, 233 Front Street (925-314-3460), which produces evening shows - e.g. 'Mortified' at 8pm - and gallery opening receptions (5:30-7:30pm), both of which release a downtown audience right into the 8-10pm window the district wants.

town_orgs.name: Visit Tri-Valley (regional destination marketing organization)
town_orgs.note: 501(c)(6) established 2005, funded by a per-room bed tax, in partnership with the cities/chambers of Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin and the Town of Danville. Programs a district can join: Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week, Wine & Dine (restaurants featuring Livermore Valley wines with waived corkage), You Sip We Ship, and Trail Passports (beer, caffeine and ice cream trails). Business listing requests via their Business Hub; sponsorship contact info@visittrivalley.

town_orgs.name: Danville Merchants' Association
town_orgs.note: Named by the Town as the organizer of the Hot Summer Sundays Car Show. No standalone website, social account or contact page found - may operate informally through the car-show organizers. Worth a direct ask via the Town's Economic Development office.

town_orgs.name: Discover Danville Association Inc.
town_orgs.note: CAUTION - appears defunct. A 501(c)(6) business league (EIN 20-2846642) of downtown Danville businesses formed to improve economic vibrancy, town centricity and tourism 'while maintaining the village atmosphere.' Last IRS filing was FY2016 (revenue -$773, net assets $0) and it is not in the IRS's most recent list of tax-exempt organizations. It historically received Town business-promotion funds. Do not build outreach plans around it without confirming it still exists. Note also that 'Discover Danville' now primarily refers to the Town's walking-tour app, and that discoverdanvilleca.com is an unrelated spam travel blog.

town_orgs.name: Museum of the San Ramon Valley
town_orgs.note: 205 Railroad Avenue (the restored 1891 Southern Pacific Depot), 925-837-3750, info@museumsrv.org. Runs Shops & Hops (the Danville craft beer stroll) and the Summer Soiree. Has a formal sponsorship program at museumsrv.org/sponsorship/. Its events are the closest existing analogue to a walkable multi-venue evening in Danville.

town_orgs.name: Danville Lions Club
town_orgs.note: Organizes 'A Taste of Danville' - the 29th annual Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk. This is the single most direct existing dine-around the district should join. Proceeds benefit Lions Club Charities, the Lions Blind Center and educational scholarships.

town_orgs.name: Kiwanis Club of San Ramon Valley
town_orgs.note: Organizes the Kiwanis-Danville 4th of July Parade with the Town. parade@srvkiwanis.org, 925-272-8207. Sponsorship tiers Presenting / Diamond / Platinum / Gold / Silver / Bronze; free parade entry at $1,000+. Mandatory entrant meeting held the preceding June.

town_orgs.name: Danville d'Elegance Foundation
town_orgs.note: Organizes the Danville Concours d'Elegance car show on Hartz & Prospect Avenues each September.

town_orgs.name: Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance (TVCCA)
town_orgs.note: Alliance of the Danville, Dublin, Livermore Valley, Pleasanton and San Ramon chambers - a route to reach industry/hospitality staff across the whole Tri-Valley for industry nights.

town_orgs.name: Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association (PCFMA)
town_orgs.note: The Town's approved operator of the Danville Farmers' Market for the last ~20 years. Market Instagram: @danvillecafm.

events.name: Danville Farmers' Market
events.when: Every Saturday, 9 a.m.-1 p.m., year-round, rain or shine
events.note: Railroad Avenue Municipal Parking Lot at the corner of Railroad and Prospect Avenues (205 Railroad Ave). Operated by PCFMA as the Town's approved operator. Instagram @danvillecafm. The most reliable weekly downtown footfall - a daytime sampling table here converts well into evening reservations.

events.name: A Taste of Danville - 29th Annual Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk
events.note: Prospect Park Plaza, 396 Hartz Ave. $45 food tasting ticket, $25 beer-and-wine pavilion; live music and dancing. Supported by the Town as part of a Council-approved program. Tickets via Eventbrite. THE most relevant existing event - a walkable multi-restaurant tasting on a weeknight in exactly the district's target hours. Contact the Danville Lions Club to be a tasting stop.

events.name: Sip & Stroll (Danville Area Chamber of Commerce)
events.note: ~35 participating businesses across downtown Danville and the Danville Livery. $65 tasting / $20 designated driver. Includes commemorative wine glass, tote bag, live music and a free trolley between downtown and the Livery. Chamber's signature event for 20+ years. Businesses apply via the 'Become a Participating Business' form emailed to events@danvilleareachamber.com.

events.name: Shops & Hops (Danville Craft Beer Stroll)
events.note: Organized by the Museum of the San Ramon Valley as a fundraiser. $35 tasting ticket, $10 designated driver. Format: participants stroll downtown shops and venues for craft beer tastings. A recent edition sold nearly all 320 tickets with 10 regional breweries pouring at 9 venues. Sponsors have included Danville Brewery, Canyon Club, Trumer Pils, Dust Bowl and The Growler.

events.name: Devil Mountain Run
events.note: Start/finish 345 Railroad Avenue, downtown Danville. USATF-certified 5K and 10K (new courses for 2026), Mile of Truth, Buddi Love Dog Mile and a free Kids Fun Run. Free tech shirts to the first 1,000 paid registrants. Organized by Team Blue Sky Events per the Town's community events list. Morning event - brunch/late-breakfast opportunity, not an 8-10pm play.

events.name: Kiwanis-Danville 4th of July Parade
events.note: Route runs Hartz Avenue and San Ramon Valley Blvd from San Ramon Valley High School at Railroad Avenue to Town & Country Drive - i.e. straight past the district. Mandatory entrants' meeting the preceding June. parade@srvkiwanis.org, 925-272-8207.

events.name: Hot Summer Sundays Car Show
events.note: Hundreds of hot rods, classics, customs and exotics line Hartz Avenue downtown, with live DJs, local vendors and food/cafe specials. Vendor and sponsor slots available - contact David, ezasugo@yahoo.com / 925-437-3649. Ends at 4pm, so the natural district play is capturing the crowd as the show breaks up.

events.name: Danville Concours d'Elegance Car Show

competitor_nightlife_zone.where: The NORTH end of downtown Danville - the 100-400 blocks of Hartz Avenue plus the Railroad Avenue / Prospect Avenue corridor, anchored by the Danville Hotel Town Center on Railroad Ave. That is roughly five to six blocks north of the district. For contrast, the four South of Hartz venues sit tightly clustered at the Hartz-and-Church corner: Incontro Ristorante 455 Hartz Ave (the historic Hartz House), Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar 480 Hartz Ave, Danville Harvest 500 Hartz Ave, and Rancho Cantina 501 Hartz Ave (the southeast corner of Hartz and Church, in the former Cocina Hermanas space). A secondary, separate late cluster sits southeast of downtown at the Danville Livery shopping center, 204 Sycamore Valley Road W, where Canyon Club Brewery runs a biergarten with firepits, heat lamps and a live-music stage.
example_venues: Elliott's Bar - 369 Hartz Ave. A dive bar in business over 100 years (briefly an ice cream parlor during Prohibition). Open 10:00 a.m. to 1:30 a.m. daily - by a wide margin the latest-closing venue in downtown Danville and the default destination after every other kitchen shuts.
Auburn Lounge & Wine Bar - 321 Hartz Ave. 1930s speakeasy feel. Mon-Wed 4 p.m.-midnight, Thu-Sun 2 p.m.-midnight.

Revel Kitchen & Bar - 331 Hartz Ave. Upscale-casual tavern from the owners of Esin, craft beer, cocktails and an eclectic wine list. Notably closes 9:00 p.m. Sun-Thu and 9:30 p.m. Fri-Sat, which is exactly the gap the district is targeting.
Danville Brewing Co. / DBC - 200 Railroad Ave, in the Danville Hotel Town Center. House beers plus guest drafts; a 2026 Diablo Magazine Best of the East Bay winner (Burger).

Crush'd Wine Bar Kitchen - downtown Danville. 24 wines on tap, craft cocktails, Apertivo Hour 3-6 p.m. daily ($12 cocktails, $9 small bites) and Live Music Thursdays. Markets itself explicitly 'from brunch to late night' - the closest direct competitor to the district's positioning.
Primo's Pizzeria & Pub - downtown; happy hour daily 3-6 p.m.
The Growler - happy hour Tuesdays 4-9 p.m., Wed-Fri 3-6 p.m.

Canyon Club Brewery - Danville Livery, 204 Sycamore Valley Rd W (separate cluster southeast of downtown). Taproom, restaurant and pilot brewery with a patio biergarten, firepits and a live-music stage.
competitor_nightlife_zone.description: Danville's noisier, younger, later-running drinking scene is concentrated at the top of Hartz Avenue and around the Danville Hotel Town Center on Railroad Ave, not at the Church Street end. The mix there is a century-old dive (Elliott's, open to 1:30 a.m.), a speakeasy-styled wine lounge (Auburn), a brewery taproom (Danville Brewing) and a self-described 'brunch to late night' wine bar (Crush'd) - venues built around drinking, standing and staying, with a beer-and-cocktail price point. The Danville Livery biergarten pulls a similar crowd off-downtown. Three things make South of Hartz's upscale-alternative positioning defensible. First, geography: the four district restaurants form a genuinely contiguous four-corner block at Hartz and Church, five-plus blocks from that cluster - close enough to be downtown, far enough to read as its own place. Second, the 8-10 p.m. gap is real and documented, not assumed: even the good sit-down rooms at the north end close at 9-9:30 p.m., and a Tri-Valley Foodist piece quoted a local observing that restaurants in Danville get all the attention, i.e. the town is restaurant-centric rather than bar-centric. Third, the district's own mix is already differentiated - a historic-house Italian room, a tiki bar, a farm-to-table kitchen and a wood-fired Mexican cantina - which supports a dinner-here, nightcap-and-dessert-there cross-visit story that a row of bars cannot tell. The realistic competitive risk is Crush'd, which already claims the late-night language, and Elliott's, which owns the after-9:30 default by simple fact of being open.

result.notes: WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM (do not treat these as established): (1) FOLLOWER COUNTS. Instagram blocks automated reads, so every follower number here comes from a search-result snippet or a cited article, not from the profile itself. The @bayarea.foodies (255K IG / 334.1K TikTok) and @daniellewalker (466K) figures come from a Diablo Magazine roundup published July 15, 2022 and are certainly stale. @danvillesocial ~11K, @danvillecagov ~15K, @danvilleharvest ~2,750 and @eastbayeats ~4,518 come from search snippets quoting the live profiles. Re-verify manually before building a media plan around any of them. (2) DANVILLE FALLFEST STATUS. Fallfest is absent from the Town's 2026 community events list and danvillefallfest.com returned no content. It may be discontinued or folded into Fall Hallo-Wine. Its historic street closures included Church Street between Railroad and Hartz - the district's own corner - so its status matters. Confirm with the chamber. (3) FALL HALLO-WINE DETAILS. I have only the Town's one-line listing (Oct 28, 2026, chamber, downtown). No dedicated event page exists yet; earlier editions ran as Flavors of Fall, Oktoberfest and Fall Rock & Stroll. (4) 2027 TASTE TRI-VALLEY DATES are unannounced; the page says to watch it. (5) CHAMBER MEMBERSHIP PRICING is not published anywhere public - the Why Join page references a Membership Toolkit but shows no tiers or dollar figures. Ask Amy Millington directly. (6) NO LOCAL PODCAST FOUND. There is no Danville CA or Tri-Valley food/nightlife podcast that I could verify. The 'Danville Podcast' on Apple Podcasts is a high-school class production from a different Danville. Treat a podcast as a gap to create rather than a channel to pitch. (7) DISCOVER DANVILLE ASSOCIATION appears defunct (last IRS filing FY2016, absent from the current IRS exempt list). 'Discover Danville' today means the Town's walking-tour web app. Also note discoverdanvilleca.com is an unrelated spam travel blog and discoverdanville.com is Danville VIRGINIA - a large share of web results for 'Danville' are Virginia, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Illinois or Indiana, so verify the state on anything not sourced here. (8) DANVILLE MERCHANTS' ASSOCIATION has no findable website or contact; it is known only from the Town's attribution of the Hot Summer Sundays Car Show. (9) HASHTAG DATA comes from best-hashtags.com co-occurrence data (a real aggregation of Instagram usage), not from Instagram directly; treat relative popularity as indicative rather than exact. (10) HOURS quoted for competitor venues come from Yelp/OpenTable listings surfaced in search and change frequently - verify before publishing any comparison. THREE FINDINGS WORTH ACTING ON FIRST: (a) The brand names are CLEAN. best-hashtags.com returns 'not found' for #danvilleafterdark, #southofhartz AND #danvillenightlife - none of the three is currently in use, so the district can own all of them outright. (b) Danville Harvest is already credited by the Town as the organizer of a downtown Neighborhood Street Party (June 20, 2026), which means one of the four partners has already walked the Town's approval path for a street-level event. (c) The Town's Economic Development Division explicitly funds 'collaborative community events,' and none of the four restaurants won a 2026 Diablo Best of the East Bay award - so there is both money and an uncontested award category available. Also flag for the site build: the Planning Commission was reviewing PERMANENT outdoor-dining rules on Sept 8, 2026 (current temporary rules expire Jan 2, 2027), and the draft explicitly PROHIBITS parklets on Hartz Avenue while capping downtown parklets at 12 spaces - directly relevant to any patio-based late-night concept.

images.description: Golden-hour storefront of the Danville location: tan/cream clapboard facade with black serif 'RANCHO CANTINA' letters on the fascia, dark reclaimed-wood beam awning with hanging bulb lights and a black lantern, two tan patio umbrellas, wood-railed deck patio with orange-slat chairs and tables, and a burnt-orange stucco planter wall in front holding agaves, a cactus and a burgundy cordyline. Clear blue sky.

Main dining room: three framed desert paintings of saguaro cactus against orange/red sunset mesas hung on a white shiplap wall, a pale-teal upholstered banquette below them, light wood tables set with amber hobnail votives and folded red-orange napkins, cream-seat wood chairs, a suspended reclaimed wood-lath ceiling raft, exposed red brick pier at right, and honey-toned plank flooring.

Booth corner: a large black metal cut-out silhouette of a vaquero on horseback swinging a lariat mounted on a white vertical-plank wall, a hammered black dome pendant with a gold interior, pale-teal banquette, butcher-block table with amber hobnail votives and orange napkins, and a framed painting of a tequila bottle at right. Clean, well-lit, simple background.

Behind the bar: a copper draft-beer tower with a row of taps set into a reclaimed-wood bar back, hand-painted ceramic tequila decanters (blue-and-white talavera style plus one black) on the shelf above, bottles of tequila and mezcal, stacked amber hobnail rocks glasses and inverted stemware below, and a bartender's arm reaching up for a bottle. Warm textured plaster wall.

Four men (team/ownership, one in a black chef's coat) standing arm-in-arm on the sidewalk in front of the Danville restaurant on a bright day. The 'RANCHO CANTINA' fascia sign, wood-railed deck, black lamp posts, terracotta pots of cactus and grasses, burnt-orange planter walls and a brick-paver crosswalk are all visible.

Overhead flat lay on a burnished copper table: a black plate with a red-sauced enchilada finished in a tight crema drizzle; a cast-iron oval skillet on a wood board holding chimichurri-topped chicken, sliced steak, grilled shrimp and zucchini; a black plate of chile relleno with rice and beans; a clear margarita with a lime wedge; a glass of dark beer; and a small dish of cucumber and jalapeno garnish beside a blue-striped kitchen towel.

Overhead taco spread on copper: two black plates of street tacos - fish tacos with cabbage slaw and chipotle drizzle, and carnitas/carne asada tacos with onion and cilantro - each with orange rice and whole beans dusted with cotija, plus a stack of warm corn tortillas, lime wedges, a red hibiscus (jamaica) drink and a beer. This is the site-wide og:image (also served from the legacy static1 path).

Wide overhead table spread on copper: a cut quesadilla with guacamole and greens, a dark plate of shredded/machaca-style beef with orange rice, saucy beans and cheesy calabacitas, a cast-iron skillet of mixed grill on a wood board, a bowl of beans with cotija and tortillas, a glass of dark beer, a lime margarita and two chile-rimmed cocktails with cucumber and jalapeno, plus a blue-striped towel.

Single plated entree shot from above on dark polished wood: a matte black plate with sliced grilled steak under a green chimichurri, orange rice, whole pinto beans dusted with cotija, a shaved fennel and herb salad, and a folded stack of warm corn tortillas. Clean subject on a simple dark background.

Overhead close-up of the wood-fired mixed grill: a cast-iron oval skillet on a wood paddle board holding chimichurri-drizzled chicken, sliced steak, grilled shrimp and a charred poblano, with a chile-salt-rimmed drink garnished with cucumber, lime and jalapeno beside it on a copper table.

Overhead on a black lattice patio table: a stainless bowl of tortilla chips flanked by a black bowl of green tomatillo salsa and one of dark red salsa, a chopped salad topped with fanned avocado, radish, corn and shredded cheese, a chile-rimmed michelada-style drink with cucumber and jalapeno, and a magenta cocktail over ice.

Tight close-up of a layered purple-and-magenta cocktail in a black hobnail-textured tumbler, garnished with a bright orange wheel, against dark green foliage bokeh. Note: this file maxes out at 667x1000 even when 2500w is requested - too small for a full-bleed hero.

Wider overhead crop of the same copper-table spread as 'Copy of untitled shoot-1494', adding a plate of crema-drizzled enchiladas with rice and beans at lower left and a magenta cocktail at upper left. Maxes out at 1000x667.

Texture/detail shot used as a full-width section background on /danville and /our-story: split oak and hardwood logs burning with tall orange flames and smoke inside the wood-fired grill. Good for a wide banner strip; no signage or people.

Scan/artwork of the printed Danville menu, page 1 - khaki-beige stock with the bracket-framed 'RANCHO CANTINA' serif wordmark, gold-tan section headings (ANTOJITOS, WOOD FIRED), small crown ornaments and vintage line-art illustrations. Menu document, not a photograph.
Scan/artwork of the printed Danville menu, page 2 (drinks and margaritas side), same beige stock and serif treatment. Menu document, not a photograph.
5x7 Taco Tuesday menu/promo card artwork used on both the Danville and Lafayette menu pages. Graphic, not a photograph.
Image of the Danville expansion press release (single page, 'alchemy' letterhead, March 2026) posted on the /danville page. A document image, not a photograph - useful as a press-kit asset only.

Gift-card promo card artwork: the full white 'RANCHO CANTINA' serif wordmark with its bracket/horn ornament set over a darkened copper-table flat lay (enchilada, mixed-grill skillet, chile relleno, margarita). The only place on the site where the complete wordmark is rendered as a raster image - useful as a wordmark reference, though it is a promo composite, not a clean logo file.

Best corner-identifying exterior: the 501 Hartz Ave building photographed from the street at golden hour after the repaint - tan/cream body with a burnt-orange accented gable and orange base wall, dark wood pergola over the side deck, tan horizontal-slat patio fence, and two black 'RANCHO CANTINA DANVILLE - COMING SOON' banners on the gable and the fence. The green 'CHURCH ST' street-name sign and a stop sign are visible at the left, with the brick-paver crosswalk in the foreground, so the Hartz Ave / Church St corner is unambiguous.

The same 501 Hartz Ave corner building BEFORE the Rancho Cantina renovation, shot from the Church St sidewalk: sage-green clapboard with white trim, wood pergola over the porch, wood railing, brick base, black lamp posts and the '501' address numerals on the stucco wall at right, hills in the distance. Photo by Jeremy Walsh for Danville San Ramon. Useful as a 'before' image only - the building has since been repainted.

Interior of the 501 Hartz space as the former Cocina Hermanas (the room Rancho Cantina took over): red-brick piers and arches, a sculpted reclaimed wood-lath ceiling, red-and-cream striped banquettes along the windows, orange and white metal cafe chairs, dark plank floor. Article caption: 'The former Cocina Hermanas. Credit: Thomas Smith'. Pre-renovation - the finished Rancho Cantina room (see image00013) has teal banquettes and a lighter floor.

ARCHITECTURAL RENDERING, not a photograph: the planned Danville storefront with a terracotta stucco entry bay, a carved wood 'Rancho Cantina' sign under gooseneck lamps, tan stucco body, cream market umbrellas over patio tables, terracotta pots and a low terracotta planter wall. Article caption: 'Rendering of the new restaurant, credit Rancho Cantina.' Do not present as a photo of the built restaurant.

Wood-fired grill in action: split logs burning under a raised steel grate with food charring on the bars, flames and sparks, and a blue-and-yellow talavera-tiled surround at right. Article credit line is 'Credit: Rancho Cantina'; the caption does not state which of the two locations it was shot in.

Wide streetscape of the Hartz Ave / Church St corner from across the intersection, pre-renovation: the low corner restaurant building with its glassed porch and pergola, bare winter trees, planters and a low white wall, with 'Church St' painted on the pavement in the foreground. Flat lighting and the road-marking angle strongly suggest a street-level survey/Street-View-style capture rather than original photography - verify licensing before use. Served as image/jpeg despite the .webp filename.

Two margaritas in hand-blown green-rimmed glasses with chile-salt rims and burnt orange wheels, on a dark wood table with a yellow patio umbrella and greenery in soft bokeh behind. Runs in Diablo magazine's Diablo Dish column on Rancho Cantina's Danville opening; alt text on the page is 'ranchocantinamargaritas.png' (supplied/courtesy image).

images.description: Straight-on daylight facade of 480 Hartz Ave: pale-yellow board-and-batten wall with a cedar-shingle bay at left, a heavy timber post-and-beam awning carrying the address numerals '480', dark-green glass double doors etched with the Kaia's mark, a carved and stained wood sign reading 'KAIA'S / ISLAND KITCHEN & TIKIBAR', a painted 'ALOHA' tiki surfboard on the shingles, a wood host stand carved with sea turtles, a concrete bench on carved-tiki legs, and bird-of-paradise and grass plantings. Clean, well-lit, unobstructed - the strongest hero for identifying the building.

The tiki bar: a full-width thatched palapa roof over the bar with bamboo framing, black-and-white mudcloth-pattern drum pendant shades, blue/red/amber/green glass float balls hung in rope netting, carved tiki totems flanking the bar, a back bar washed in magenta and purple light and stacked with rum and spirits, wall-mounted screens playing reef and beach footage, a red-lit bar rail with mismatched vintage metal stools, and the painted sunset-beach mural continuing on the left wall.

Wide interior looking down the length of the room: bamboo ceiling framing and a painted-sky ceiling at left, woven lauhala and bamboo wall panels, high-tops with teal and orange stools, the hand-painted sunset-palms beach mural on the end wall, a thatched canopy and a tall carved tiki post at centre, and the working bar at right with copper mule mugs, shakers and a galvanized tub of glassware in the foreground.

The signature wall mural - a hand-painted sunset over a beach with palm trees, orange sky and a low sun on the water - behind a row of wood high-top tables with teal and orange stools, a carved wood wainscot band, woven wall panels, framed tropical art and tiki masks at left, a bamboo pendant with a printed shade, and a tall carved tiki totem in the right foreground. Site caption: 'Wall mural depicting a beach and palm trees.'

Sunlit garden patio: a grey steel pergola strung with festoon lights and hung with overhead heaters, teak-slat chairs and speckled granite-top tables on a concrete terrace, a cedar-shingle wall behind, raised concrete and redwood planters full of red mandevilla, bird-of-paradise and palms, and a few steps down to the street. Site caption: 'Outdoor dining area.'

Covered sidewalk patio running along Hartz Ave: a white soffit trimmed with split-bamboo poles, dark ceiling fans and infrared wall heaters, a bar-height rail counter along the street edge, speckled granite tables with red napkins and water glasses, a tall bamboo hedge screening the windows, and parked cars, street lamps and the tree-lined avenue beyond. Site caption: 'The exterior covered patio.'

The 'Kaia's Beach Hut' dining room: a freestanding bamboo-and-thatch hut structure built inside the room with a round carved sign reading 'Kaia's BEACH HUT', thatch eaves, a woven mat ceiling with Edison bulbs and a turquoise glass float, woven lauhala walls with carved wood panels and framed vintage beach prints, a surfboard on the wall, and mint-green metal cafe chairs at wood tables set with red napkins and candles. Site caption: 'A large dining hall.'

Tiki lounge nook: a large carved bamboo-framed relief panel of a turquoise island scene on the wall, a striped daybed sofa piled with coral and teal tropical-print pillows, a rattan armchair with a red hibiscus cushion, a surfboard-shaped coffee table on black hairpin legs, two rope-wrapped drum stools, a sisal rug, a small coral-shaded lamp and a galvanized ice bucket at left. Site caption: 'The lounge area with various decorations.'

The outdoor fire-pit table set with the full menu: a long teak table with a black lava-rock fire trough down the middle, ringed by dishes including loco moco with a fried egg, an ahi poke bowl with fanned avocado and edamame, a seared salmon plate, a Big Island cobb salad, a yellow curry with rice and an orchid, tuna crisps/tostadas with a dipping sauce, and a chocolate lava cake, plus a carved Kaia's tiki mug, a blue Hawaii in a hurricane glass and a mai tai. Site caption: 'Various food on the fire pit table.'

'Aloha Feast' - a wood table laid with nine plates against the red palm-print banquette: loco moco with a fried egg, an ahi poke bowl, a seared salmon over rice with a banana leaf, a black plate of tuna/ahi tostadas with a flower, salmon over black rice and slaw, a yellow shrimp curry with rice and an orchid, tuna crisps, and a chocolate dessert - plus a carved Kaia's tiki mug, a branded rocks glass with mint, a tall tiki-glyph glass and a blue Hawaii in a hurricane glass.

Ahi tuna poke bowl in a periwinkle-blue ceramic bowl on a wood table: cubed marinated ahi, a scoop of white rice with furikake on a banana leaf, edamame, pickled red onion, julienned carrot and cucumber, mango salsa and a fanned avocado, with a red palm-print banquette behind and a Kaia's-branded glass at right. Site caption: 'Ahi tuna poke bowl.'

Overhead of three fish tacos on a white plate over a banana leaf - white fish with pineapple salsa, purple cabbage, avocado and micro-greens - with three lime wedges and a mound of pineapple coleslaw, on a wood table beside a rattan chair. Site caption: 'Fish tacos, with pineapple salsa, cabbage, lime, avocado, and a side of pineapple coleslaw.'

Tall tiki highball printed with orange-and-black Polynesian glyphs, filled with crushed ice and a rose-coloured drink, garnished with a purple orchid and a long pandan/ti leaf, set on a yellow coaster on a wood table with the red-and-teal tropical-palm-print banquette filling the background. Site caption: 'Tiki cocktail.'

Mai tai in a rocks glass printed with the gold 'KAIA'S / ISLAND KITCHEN & TIKI BAR' logo and tiki glyphs, topped with crushed ice, a big mint bouquet and a lime wheel, on a wood table beside a woven rattan chair and a carved tiki side table with a turquoise planter. Site caption: 'Mai Tai cocktail with mint.' Branded glassware makes this a good logo-bearing detail shot.

The site's og:image: a crisp-skinned salmon fillet topped with micro-greens over white rice with broccolini, carrots and a banana-leaf garnish on a white plate, dotted with chilli oil and green herb powder, on a wood table with a red napkin, the red palm-print banquette behind and a carved orange tiki mug at upper right.

Elevated/drone still looking down Hartz Avenue in downtown Danville, used as the homepage video poster: brick-paver crosswalk and sidewalk bulb-outs, angled parking, a full sycamore canopy over the street, shop awnings and street lamps, and Kaia's blue monument sign and covered patio visible mid-frame on the right. Good neighbourhood/streetscape banner; it shows the block rather than the restaurant close-up.

Six women in flower leis, floral maxi dresses and a flower crown posed sitting and crouching on the concrete bench directly beneath the carved wood 'KAIA'S / ISLAND KITCHEN & TIKIBAR' sign on the yellow board-and-batten wall, framed by large bird-of-paradise leaves. Site caption: 'Several people posing outside in front of the restaurant.' Good for a 'celebrations/parties' slot; contains identifiable guests.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Seafood with Thai green curry and rice.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot (wood table, tropical-print banquette background).
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Grilled salmon on a bed of rice, with sauteed veggies and oil.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Big Island Cobb Salad.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Loco Moco.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Vegetable Garlic Noodle.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Spam Musubi.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Poke Crisp.' Single-dish studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.
Restaurant's own gallery caption: 'Chocolate Lava Cake.' Dessert studio shot from the same in-house food shoot.

Primary logo file: the all-caps 'KAIA'S' wordmark in a heavy, slightly distressed dark-olive serif on a transparent PNG background. Small (262x57) - this is the only logo raster the site serves, so it will need vector re-creation for large-format use.

Highest-resolution exterior available: golden-hour view from the Hartz Ave sidewalk of the blue surfboard-shaped monument sign reading 'KAIA'S - ISLAND KITCHEN & TIKI BAR' in gold, set in a sand-and-river-rock garden with palms, succulents and red flowering plants, with the covered pergola patio full of diners, patio heaters and the cedar-shingle building behind, under big sycamores. Credit Thomas Smith / Bay Area Telegraph. Contains identifiable guests.

Kaia's from the Hartz Ave sidewalk on a bright day: the blue 'KAIA'S - ISLAND KITCHEN & TIKI BAR' monument sign in its sand-and-rock planting bed with palms and succulents, the grey steel pergola patio with heaters and umbrellas behind, a smaller 'KAIA'S' sign on the building, a US flag on the lamp post, brick-paver sidewalk and sycamore shade. Few people, clean framing.

Second exterior angle from the same review: the blue Kaia's monument sign closer and lower, showing the bronze sea-turtle sculpture and river-rock feature in the planting bed, with the pergola patio and seated guests behind and the residential street beyond. Credit Bay Area Telegraph. Contains identifiable guests.

A pale-gold frozen tropical drink (pina-colada / painkiller style) in a hurricane glass with a black straw and a pineapple wedge, sitting on the sidewalk-patio rail counter with Hartz Avenue, parked cars and a storefront awning in soft focus behind. Credit Bay Area Telegraph.

Detail shot of a round pulp-paper coaster on a speckled granite bar top, printed with the gold 'KAIA'S' wordmark, 'ISLAND KITCHEN & TIKI BAR' and a web address. Useful as a branded-detail image; note the coaster in this photo carries a misspelled URL ('kaiasdanvillle.com', three l's) so avoid using it anywhere the address must be legible. Credit Bay Area Telegraph.

Bright turquoise Blue Hawaii-style cocktail in a footed hurricane glass, capped with crushed ice and garnished with a pineapple wedge and a maraschino cherry, on a wood table against blurred palm foliage. Runs in Diablo magazine's Diablo Dish column; the page's alt text credits it 'Courtesy Kaia's'. CAUTION: the rendering of the glass, ice and foliage looks stylised/synthetic rather than like the rest of Kaia's photography - confirm provenance with the restaurant before publishing.

images.description: Golden-hour three-quarter view of the corner building: the glassed-in wraparound porch with white-mullioned windows and a weathered wood frame, a large distressed metal sign reading 'harvest' in white lowercase mounted across the glass, purple market umbrellas and string lights above the shingled hip roof, a stucco knee-wall base, and a raised bed of blooming lavender and ornamental grasses along the sidewalk, with a big sycamore trunk framing the left edge. Site alt text: 'Danville Harvest Exterior'.

Wide dusk view of the whole restaurant from across Hartz Avenue: the pale-yellow Queen Anne cottage with its shingled hip roof and gabled porch, the glassed porch with the 'harvest' sign, navy market umbrellas over the side patio, string lights, an American flag on the corner post, a blue USPS collection box and a wine barrel on the far sidewalk, mature sycamores overhead, a brick-paver crosswalk in the foreground and the Las Trampas hills on the horizon. Site alt text: 'The view of Danville Harvest as seen from across the street.'

Blue-hour exterior of the same corner: the building lit warm from inside, the illuminated 'harvest' sign glowing on the glass porch, uplit lavender and grass plantings, navy umbrellas and string lights, a lit patio to the left, sycamores in silhouette against a deep blue sky, and the crosswalk and red-painted kerb in the foreground.

The side patio at night: a run of pale-yellow clapboard wall with tall white french doors glowing from inside, a white retractable awning, festoon lights and a row of infrared wall heaters overhead, wood-slat tables and chairs on the terrace, a weathered picket fence and ornamental grasses along the street edge, and deep blue dusk sky. Site alt text: 'The side patio area as seen at night.'

Back dining room: a grey button-tufted banquette against a herringbone reclaimed-wood feature wall hung with two round mirrors, sconces and small framed prints; tan leather nailhead chairs and a blue tufted booth, light wood tables with pink peonies in bud vases and rolled napkins, black dome pendant lamps, tall white-mullioned windows with floor-length linen curtains and a polished concrete floor. Site alt text: 'Our main dining area in the back of our restaurant. Great for private events.'

Front dining room with the full bar: a thick wood bar top with a steel rail running across the foreground, olive-green upholstered swivel stools, suspended steel-mesh glass racks over the bar, a caramel leather banquette along the back wall with wood tables, reclaimed barn-wood panelling, a small chandelier, pendant lamps, curtained windows and a hanging pothos. Site alt text: 'The view of our front dining area with full bar and tables.'

The bar shot straight down its length: a long polished wood bar top with olive-green swivel stools, a tiered back bar of whiskey and spirits under warm shelf lighting, suspended steel-mesh stemware racks, a wall-mounted screen, a small oak barrel, a brass tap and a service sink, glass-front wine and beverage coolers glowing blue under the counter, and a dark, moody overall key.

Long view down the dining room aisle: tan leather nailhead chairs at light wood tables set with pink peonies, folded grey napkins and cutlery; a white-tiled wall with a glazed pass-through shelf of stacked plates and glassware at left; black dome pendants; heavy linen curtains rope-tied to wood posts; blue tufted booths at right; polished concrete floor. Site alt text: 'Back Dining Area'.

Vertical/portrait interior: the dining room seen past a curtain and a glass partition, with black dome pendants in a row, linen curtains, a herringbone wood wall with round mirrors and sconces at the far end, a blue tufted booth at left and caramel leather chairs at set tables with pink peonies. Portrait orientation makes this useful for mobile or a tall card. Site alt text: 'Our back dining area. Perfect for private parties.'

Vertical interior: a row of tables with pink peonies in glass bud vases, rolled grey napkins and cutlery, tan leather nailhead chairs, black dome pendants, tied-back linen curtains and, over the far doorway, a large weathered sign reading 'COOK'. result.description: Incontro Ristorante is an upscale-casual Italian restaurant in the historic Hartz House at 455 Hartz Ave in downtown Danville, serving regional Italian cooking across a garden patio, a covered veranda and stone-walled indoor dining rooms. The restaurant's own words: "Incontro is a place where family and friends come together to share meaningful moments. Inspired by the rich culinary heritage of Italy, our name reflects the spirit of gathering and connection. We bring diverse flavors from all regions of Italy to the heart of Danville." (incontrodanville.com). Bread, pasta and desserts are made in house; the kitchen runs handmade gnocchi, lasagne, lobster ravioli, a four-pasta "Chef's Taste of Italy" plate, plus seafood and steak secondi. There is an indoor and outdoor full bar, live music on the patio in the warmer months, a Sunday all-you-can-eat brunch buffet plus a Saturday midday buffet, a 16-seat Wine Room for private dining and a full tray catering menu. Albi's Middle Eastern Beer Garden, run by the owners' daughter Monique Moufarrej, occupies the back of the same 455 Hartz Ave property.

result.notes:
NAME AND ADDRESS CONFIRMED. The exact name is "Incontro Ristorante" (the OpenTable listing shortens it to "Incontro Restaurant"). The address is 455 Hartz Ave, Danville, CA 94526 — NOT the Church St corner. It sits on the west side of Hartz between Church St and Railroad Ave, in the building OpenStreetMap independently names "Hartz House," which matches the restaurant's own claim of dining "in the historic Hartz House." Nearby-business check from the vrconcierge listing: Danville Harvest at 500 Hartz Ave (210 ft), Cocina Hermanas at 501 Hartz Ave (220 ft) and Bridges Restaurant & Bar at 44 Church St (229 ft). Note the brief's premise about "Rancho Cantina at 501 Hartz" — 501 Hartz is now listed as Cocina Hermanas. I did not verify Kaia's Island Kitchen at 480 Hartz.

SISTER RESTAURANT: Albi's Middle Eastern Beer Garden occupies the back of the same 455 Hartz Ave property, opened April 24 2026, run by Monique Moufarrej (daughter of Incontro's owners; CIA graduate, ex-Del Posto, ex-Rich Table, ex-Angler SF). Hours Wed–Sun 11:30 AM–8:00 PM. Site: albisdanville.com, Instagram @albis_danville. Incontro's homepage carries an Albi's promo block and one Albi's food photo (a Middle Eastern mezze spread at https://www.incontrodanville.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/652769770_17927523081239109_227673107610504758_n.jpg) — I excluded it from the images array because it is Albi's food, not Incontro's.

MENU SOURCE: the website's "Menu" and "view all menu" links both point to the boons.io ordering site, which is the live, current menu — the price widget embedded on the homepage is stale (it shows Bruschetta at $24 and $16 where the live menu says $16; vegan pastas at $26 where the live menu says $27). All dish prices I reported come from the live ordering menu.

DATA I COULD NOT GET, and why: (1) OpenTable — both WebFetch and curl timed out repeatedly against opentable.com from this environment, so I have no OpenTable rating, review count, dress code, parking or executive-chef field; the reservation URL comes from the restaurant's own homepage link. (2) Yelp — returns HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl. Search-result page titles show "591 Reviews, 626 Photos" as of August 2026 but I could not read the star rating off the page, so yelp_rating is left empty rather than guessed. (3) Instagram — instagram.com/incontro_ristorante returns a JavaScript shell with no bio text in the HTML, so no bio captured. (4) Facebook — facebook.com/INCONTRODANVILLE returned HTTP 400 to curl and only the page title to WebFetch. (5) The homepage has NO og:image meta tag, so og_image is empty. (6) No current executive-chef name is published anywhere I could read. (7) No dedicated private-dining page exists; private events live in a homepage section, so private_dining_url is empty — the Eventective third-party listing (100-guest max, 16-seat Wine Room, events phone 925-548-7778, $500–$5,000/event) is the most detailed source.

OTHER SOCIAL: the restaurant also links X/Twitter @INCONTRO455 (https://x.com/INCONTRO455) from its site footer. No TikTok found. The footer's "Facebook"/"Instagram" icons on some templates point to bare facebook.com / instagram.com placeholders; the real handles are in the header and are the ones I reported.

SITE-QUALITY CAVEAT for anyone re-scraping: the WordPress theme ("Basilico") still has unedited demo content in places — the catering page shows fake sister locations in Sydney, Tokyo and New York with a placeholder phone +(406) 555-0120 and Basilicofood123@gmail.com, and the footer carries a leftover "Andé Restaurant, 767 5th Avenue, Paris" block and lorem ipsum. None of that is real. Likewise, the homepage's lead exterior image is an AI-generated ChatGPT render, flagged in the images array.

EVENTS/PROMOS observed in the site media library (2026): monthly 10%-off online-order promo codes (LABOR10, TREAT10, SUMMER10, TGIF10, SPECIAL10, FREEDOM10, BESTDAD), holiday prix-fixe PDFs (Valentine's, Easter brunch, Mother's Day, Father's Day brunch, Christmas Eve, New Year's Eve, Thanksgiving) and a wine-dinner series — e.g. "Incontro Presents O'Neill's Wine Dinner, Thursday March 12, 2026, 6:30 pm, $145 per person plus tax and gratuity," a five-course menu with Robert Hall and Ram's Gate pairings (graphic at https://www.incontrodanville.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/A43BE9B2-052B-4129-9EFD-5F4FFCCED4B5.jpg).

IMAGE METHOD: I pulled raw HTML for the homepage and catering page with curl, extracted img src / srcset / data-src / CSS background-image / og:image, resolved relative URLs and stripped WordPress size suffixes to reach the originals; I then enumerated the full media library via the WordPress REST API (wp-json/wp/v2/media, 116 items across 2 pages) to catch photos not currently placed on a page and to read the alt text. Every URL in the images array was checked with curl -sIL (all returned HTTP 200 with the content-type and content-length recorded) and then downloaded and measured with Pillow for true width/height. Theme demo/stock assets (anything titled "Basilico", plus the unsplash and pexels files) were excluded. No Instagram or Facebook CDN URLs are included, and no Yelp or Google user photos were needed — every image is first-party on incontrodanville.com.
